claims.statement: Muratov-Novaga (arXiv:2610.29732v1), p. 4, Theorem 1: among Bravais lattices of covolume one the BCC lattice is the unique minimiser of the Born Coulombic energy E(L) = E(L, 1/2). Lattice-restricted; the non-periodic problem is not covered.
Muratov-Novaga (arXiv:2610.29732v1), p. 13, Proposition 6: the bisection terminates and covers the parameter rectangle by 46 414 closed boxes, each verified by one of four tests (R), (C), (B), (E).
Luo-Wei (arXiv:2610.31456v1), p. 2, Theorem 1.1 item (2): for the 3D Yukawa energy among lattices of covolume one and 0 < kappa < kappa_*, the BCC lattice is the unique minimiser. Lattice-only.

Rougerie-Serfaty (arXiv:1307.2805v5), p. 12, Theorem 1: for every dimension d >= 2 the infimum of the renormalized energy over A_1 is achieved and finite, with a periodic minimising sequence (for the energy W of their (2.16)-(2.17)).

Blanc-Lewin (arXiv:1504.01153v2), section 2.6, p. 19: for d = 3 numerical simulations indicate BCC is the global minimiser of the Coulomb lattice energy as conjectured by Wigner, 'Proving this fact is still an open problem'; BCC -1.44423 and FCC -1.44415 (times rho^{1/3}); Lieb-Narnhofer prove e_Jell(rho) >= -1.4508 rho^{1/3}, an argument that 'is still an open problem' to close to BCC (quotation).

Lewin (arXiv:2202.09240v2), Remark 19, p. 22: in d = 3 the Onsager-type constant is c1 = (3/5)(9 pi/2)^{1/3} ~ 1.4508, close to the conjectured best value 1.4442. The original Lieb-Narnhofer paper was not opened.

Aydin-Iacobelli (arXiv:2610.28547v1), p. 4: lattice results on the quantization problem do not settle Gersho's conjecture, 'which remains open for d >= 3'. The Kelvin/Weaire-Phelan, Barnes-Sloane, Choksi-Lu and HS26 statements are taken from that paper's text (p. 4-6) and are second-hand here.

Rougerie-Serfaty (arXiv:1307.2805v5), Remark B.2, p. 67: for d >= 3 the cutoff-based renormalized energy W of (2.16)-(2.17) 'may depend on the choice of cutoff', unlike d = 2; so the 2D statement 'for every field in A_1' has no verified 3D counterpart (the statement about the minimum transfers through Theorem 1, B3-L-0004).

Muratov-Novaga (arXiv:2610.29732v1): the relative BCC-FCC energy gap is 6.2e-5 (p. 3); Section 7 (p. 14) calls the non-periodic BCC problem 'a substantially harder three-dimensional crystallization problem'.

Hales-McLaughlin (arXiv:math/9811079v3), abstract only: the volume of a Voronoi polyhedron in a unit-ball packing is at least that of a regular dodecahedron of unit inradius. The dodecahedron is not a tiling cell, so this per-cell bound is not sharp at the optimal packing (our inference; ABSTRACT AND FIRST PAGE ONLY were read).

Dual identity (3D transcription). Let h solve -Delta h = 4 pi (sum_p delta_p - 1) on a periodic configuration, W(h) = (1/8 pi) int^ren |grad h|^2 (unit density, per-particle units). For any trial H with the same 1/r singularities at the sites, u = h - H: int|grad h|^2 = int|grad u|^2 + 2 int grad h . grad H - int|grad H|^2, and int grad h . grad H = 4 pi (H_reg(0) - int H) by the equation for h. Hence W(h) = F(H) + (1/8 pi) int|grad(h - H)|^2 with F(H) = sum_cells [ -int H - (1/8 pi) int^ren |grad H|^2 ] (constant term of the singular expansion normalised to zero). F(H) <= W(h) for every admissible H, with equality iff H = h. The renormalisation bookkeeping at the sites is inherited from the 2D proof and is not re-derived here.

Slack lemma. (i) Pointwise: if grad H(x) lies in a linear subspace N(x) for every H in the class, then |grad(h - H)|^2 >= |P_{N(x)^perp} grad h|^2 (Pythagoras; a linear subspace is all that is used); for H = H(r) this is the tangential gradient, for axial H(r, angle to n) it is (e_psi . grad h)^2. (ii) Isometry: if R is an isometry of a piece preserving the Dirichlet form and the singular part, and H = H o R, then (1 - R)(h - H) = (1 - R) h, and since ||(1 - R)/2|| <= 1 in the Dirichlet norm, ||grad(h - H)|| >= ||grad (h - h o R)/2||. (iii) Squared Dirichlet distances add over pieces with disjoint interiors, and the maximum of two valid lower bounds is valid.

Ceiling lemma. Suppose a method certifies, for every configuration to which the method applies (in the planar architecture: separated configurations, G13), F(H_conf) >= C N for trial potentials H_conf in a class K (so that the certified constant is C). Applied to the BCC torus, C <= F(H_bcc)/N = W_bcc - (1/8 pi) int|grad(h_bcc - H_bcc)|^2 <= W_bcc - inf_{H in K} slack(H). This does not use that BCC is the minimiser. BCC is separated (nearest-neighbour distance (sqrt(3)/2) 2^{1/3} ~ 1.091 > R ~ 0.620), so the lemma applies to it.

Why exact calibration works in 2D and fails for the 3D transcription. 2D: in each Voronoi sector h_tri = gamma(r) + sum_m c_m r^{6m} T_{6m}(d/t) because cos(6 m phi) = T_{6m}(d/t); so h_tri is a function of (r, t) only, lies in the sector ansatz class, and the square term is zero. 3D: the axial ansatz H(r, theta) restricted to a face (r = t) is a function of t = sqrt(d^2 + rho^2) alone, hence constant on every circle of fixed in-face radius rho. If h_bcc is not constant on such a circle, then H != h_bcc and the square term is strictly positive. The 2D statement is the manuscript identity as audited in the P1 audit; it is not re-checked here.

Cell Euler identity. A convex polyhedron with f faces, e edges, v vertices has v - e + f = 2 and every vertex has degree >= 3, so 3v <= 2e, e <= 3f - 6, sum_F n_F = 2e <= 6f - 12, i.e. sum_F (6 - n_F) >= 12, with equality iff the cell is simple (every vertex of degree 3). For a simple cell sum_F (6 - n_F) = 12 exactly, whatever f is. (FCC rhombic dodecahedron: f = 12, e = 24, sum (6 - n_F) = 24.)

Transfer of the 2D incidence count (sketch). Give each in-face sector (face F, edge e) the weight K (3 theta'_e/pi - 1) with theta'_e the signed in-face angle at the foot. A face whose foot is inside sums to K (6 - n_F); a foot outside gives -K n_F >= K (6 - n_F) when K <= 0. Tiny faces at near-degenerate vertices force K <= 0 (J -> 0 while the weight stays fixed). So the count transfers with K <= 0 and uses only the identity B3-C-0014, after one extra step. Unlike 2D, the Euler inequality sum_F (6 - n_F) >= 12 points in the unfavourable direction for K <= 0 (non-simple cells such as those of fcc and hcp give 24 K). The transfer therefore uses an extra step: configurations with simple Voronoi cells are dense, and W_N is continuous on separated configurations, so it suffices to prove the bound for simple tessellations, on which sum_F (6 - n_F) = 12 exactly; the certificate domain must then include a margin below the separation distance (as the planar proof's b = 0.28209 < d_* does) to cover nearby perturbations. Not carried out in detail.

Screened potential and separation in 3D. With R = (3/(4 pi))^{1/3} (ball of volume 1) and phi(x) = 1/|x| - 3/(2R) + |x|^2/(2R^3) on B_R: phi(R) = 1/R - 3/(2R) + 1/(2R) = 0, phi'(R) = -1/R^2 + 1/R^2 = 0, and -Delta phi = 4 pi delta - 3/R^3 = 4 pi (delta - 1_{B_R}) because 3/(4 pi R^3) = 1. By the same strict-minimum-principle argument as in 2D (r_* = 1/sqrt(pi)) this suggests separation >= R ~ 0.6204 and face distance >= R/2 ~ 0.3102 for a minimiser. The identities are checked by hand; the transfer of the minimum-principle step is asserted, not written out.

Additive invariants of a simple cell. From v = 2f - 4 and sum n_F = 6f - 12: a f + b sum n_F + c v = (a + 6 b + 2 c) f - 12 b - 4 c, which is the same for all simple cells iff a + 6 b + 2 c = 0. So, besides volume and total solid angle, there is a one-parameter family of count weights (one free constant), i.e. three multipliers (lambda, mu, K) in total.

Calibration count (heuristic, NOT a theorem; it is the only argument against classes whose data are not invariant under the 60-degree rotation of the hexagonal pyramids, whatever their number of parameters). The truncated octahedron has 144 flags and the group O_h has order 48, so 3 flag orbits (assuming the action on flags is free); each in-face sector (face, edge) pairs two mirror flags, so there are 3 sector types: (square face, hex-square edge), (hex face, hex-square edge), (hex face, hex-hex edge). Piece-intrinsic data see 2 types (square, hex); neighbour data split the hex type in two. A per-piece affine bound tight at the optimum imposes, per type, three stationarity conditions and one equality, i.e. about 8 conditions (2 types) or 12 (3 types), against 3 multipliers. In 2D: 1 sector type, 2 stationarity conditions and 1 equality = 3 against 3. Hidden identities from the stationarity of W at BCC are not excluded.

2D baseline as described by the openai/math preprint 'Triangular minimality for planar Coulomb renormalized energy' (AI-generated, not peer reviewed) and by our independent reproduction and audit (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23653827): reduction to square tori (SS2012), existence of a torus minimiser with separation, glued sector trial potential and dual identity, exact calibration at the triangular lattice, stationarity of two multipliers, a finite certificate. This paper takes the 2D proof as given (the audit found no gap in Sections 2-5) and did not re-read the manuscript ourselves at paper stage; the step descriptions follow FEASIBILITY.md section 2. An independent AI audit of this preprint re-read 04-calibration.tex (Lemmas cal:stationarity, cal:energy-identity, eq. cal:trial-potential) and found the description of G5-G9 accurate.

Residual plan (a weaker target, not optimality). Prove by computer assistance a 3D jellium lower bound W >= W_bcc - delta* with delta* as small as the ceiling of B3-C-0012 allows, using the 3D dual identity with the axial ansatz. First lemma: the 3D torus pipeline (separation R, axial dual identity on flat tori of volume N, in-face signed-sector reduction to a three-variable primitive Gamma_{d,s}(x)). Falsification test, to run first: (1) optimise the axial radial data B, D_k to maximise the calibrated constant 12 K + lambda + 4 pi mu; (2) sample random in-face sectors (d >= 0.31, s and x arbitrary) and check that the piece inequality holds; (3) kill the plan if the best feasible constant does not beat the radial-only ceiling, i.e. if the angular modes add nothing. Not run.

Certificate-size estimate under stated assumptions. 2D record: outer mesh about 2184 x 3611 nodes, Hessian mesh about 2.4e6 cells, global-derivative mesh about 4.2e5 rectangles, 72.6 s on 32 threads (about 2.3e3 core-s). Assumptions: (a) best case, exact axial pieces with a primitive in 3 variables; (b) margins scale with the relative gap of the nearest competitor, 8.0e-3 in 2D against 6.2e-5 in 3D (factor 129); (c) interpolation error proportional to h^2, so 11.4 times finer per dimension; (d) the same cost per node. Under (a)-(d): uniform mesh (2808 x 11.4)^3 ~ 3.2e13 nodes ~ 2e2 core-years; five parameters: ~ 3e22 nodes. Adaptive boxes (cf. 46 414 boxes in Muratov-Novaga) make 1e5-1e8 plausible IF a sharp piece inequality existed.

Ewald jellium energies per particle at unit density (1/r Coulomb, uniform background; fcc-bcc gap computed from these energies, 8.969202e-5, and 2 x gap = 1.793840e-4 matches Muratov-Novaga's 1.7938403e-4): bcc -1.4442307515, fcc -1.4441410595 (gap 8.969e-5), hcp -1.4440838423 (gap 1.469e-4), sc -1.4186487397, A15 -1.4408630487, C15 -1.4284766566. Positive controls: independence of the Ewald splitting parameter to <= 9e-16; literature Madelung constants (Wigner-Seitz units) reproduced to 2.8e-13 (bcc, fcc, hcp) and 2.1e-9 (sc). Negative control: dropping the background term makes the result depend on the splitting parameter (spread 0.44).

Periodic Voronoi statistics over 32 configurations (lattices, A15, C15, perturbed bcc/fcc/hcp, two Poisson samples): mean faces bcc 14, fcc 12, hcp 12, A15 13.5, C15 13.33, sc 6, perturbed fcc about 14, Poisson 15.5. Mean sum_F (6 - n_F) = 12 in 29 of the 32; fcc and hcp (non-simple cells) give 24 (negative control for the 'simple cell' hypothesis); one perturbed hcp run gave 11.9375, which is impossible for convex cells and is attributed (by us, not independently verified) to a near-degenerate-vertex merge at the 1e-7 tolerance. Second moment G: bcc 0.0785433 < A15 0.0787354 < fcc 0.0787451 = hcp < C15 0.0793381 < sc 0.0833333.

Sanity checks on the bcc Green function h used in the slack bounds: finite-difference Laplacian off the sites 12.5656 against 4 pi = 12.5664; gradient against central differences, max deviation 9.0e-9; cubic-harmonic fit near the site gives regular constant C = -2.88847 against 2 x Madelung = -2.88846 (positive control), and the degree-4 coefficient c4 = -2.77 (bcc), -1.55 (fcc), +7.60 (sc).

Face traces of h_bcc on circles of fixed in-face radius (rho/inradius = 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, i.e. fixed t): hexagonal face max-min = 8.9e-6, 5.7e-4, 6.6e-3, only azimuthal mode cos 6 psi (amplitude 3.3e-3 at 0.9), all other modes up to 8 below 7e-17; square face only cos 4 psi (5.9e-3 at 0.9) and cos 8 psi. So the trace is not a function of t alone.

Lower bounds on the square term (1/8 pi) int |grad(h_bcc - H)|^2 per particle by Sobol quasi-Monte Carlo over the BCC cell (two seeds, 11 and 12): radial class 3.091e-3; axial class (max(pair-average bound, azimuthal bound) on hex pyramids plus azimuthal bound on square pyramids) 1.058e-4 (seed 11 1.0586e-4, seed 12 1.0576e-4); piece-intrinsic hierarchical class on hexagonal pyramids only 8.751e-5 (8.7547e-5, 8.7477e-5), about 300 standard errors from zero. Positive control: replacing h by the exactly radial Wigner-Seitz field gives <= 2.2e-30 for all bounds. The study's own control does not test the rotation convention of the pair-average bound (a radial field is invariant under any rotation). Independent-auditor result (AUDIT.md, auditor script /tmp/b3audit/ctl.py, not re-run by the writer; paper's own bounds_for_gradient, 2^16 Sobol points, seed 5, one hexagonal pyramid): R-invariant non-radial field (n.x)^3 + rho^4: hierarchical 5.4e-35, axial 3.9e-36 (full Dirichlet 1.28e-3); cos 6 psi: hierarchical 3.0e-37, axial 2.8e-7; cos 3 psi (odd under R): hierarchical 1.29994e-4 = its full Dirichlet energy 1.29994e-4, as predicted; the rotation convention in the code is correct.

Consequence (ceilings, B3-C-0012 evaluated with B3-X-0005): any certified constant from a trial class that is radial, axial or piece-intrinsic hierarchical (hexagonal pyramids) satisfies C <= W_bcc - 3.09e-3 (radial), C <= W_bcc - 1.06e-4 (axial), C <= W_bcc - 8.75e-5 (hierarchical). Scale: 8.75e-5 is 0.98 x and 1.06e-4 is 1.18 x the fcc-bcc gap (8.969e-5), and 0.72 x the hcp-bcc gap for the axial one; the radial ceiling is 34.5 x the gap. None of these is zero, which is what kills exact calibration. Square pyramids are not used in the hierarchical bound (a larger bound is expected).

2D reference: the radial-class slack for h_tri (series of the manuscript, 400000 Monte Carlo points) is 1.85e-3, which is 0.056 x the 2D square-minus-triangular gap 0.03325; the 2D sector class has slack 0 by the manuscript identity (a constant in the script, not a computed value; see B3-C-0019). The 2D lattice energies are typed constants; the 2D reference is plain Monte Carlo with no standard error (MC hexagon area 1.0011).

Residual-plan scale: the radial ceiling W_bcc - 3.09e-3 = -1.4473 is above the Lieb-Narnhofer value -1.4508 by 3.5e-3 (the LN gap to BCC is 6.6e-3), so a radial-class calibration could in principle improve on LN by at most about 3.5e-3, and the axial class leaves at most 1.06e-4 from BCC; these are ceilings on what the method could deliver, not bounds that we have obtained.
